title: Feature and dossier hubs lag the roadmap: closed stages described as planning, blocked or not closed
affected_invariant: Authority hierarchy: roadmap (S01) decides status; hubs must not contradict it
impact: EVOL_X hubs say W1 only, 'no change_safety code until W2', 'W2 not auto-authorized', while EVOL-X is CLOSED on the roadmap and testing_support/change_safety exists at SHA. MCP_SERVER hubs say 'stage not CLOSED' and 'P2+ Blocked' while MCP-SERVER-X is CLOSED (2026-11-12). SCENARIO_FACTORY plan says ADR-SFX-001..006 'not yet published' and T-IGX-037-B..E 'Planned' while SFX_INDEX records them Published. TOKEN cache-prefix addendum header says runtime wiring is planned while its own sections 6/7 describe as-built, accepted runtime. PDC_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX header still says 'draft for architecture lock (OD-PDC-ADR-01 pending)' while PDC_INDEX marks it Locked. The hubs are the entry points for agents (README), so stale status misleads implementation and audit sessions.
recommendation: Stage owners reduce each hub to a status-neutral pointer to the dossier/roadmap row or update the status block; for the PDC matrix header, align with PDC_INDEX at the next PDC-X docs batch (PDC is in flight, so no verdict implied).
owner: EVOL-X / MCP-SERVER-X / SFX / PDC-X doc owners
decision_authority: Roadmap owner (Operator) for status wording; stage owners for edits

title: Capability architecture files without plan pairs, and a pair gate that only checks README-indexed features
affected_invariant: capabilities/README rule 3: every architecture file has a matching plan file
evidence: E1:git ls-tree shows capabilities/architecture holds 10 files, capabilities/plan holds 7; missing plan sides: PROOF_DATA_PACKAGE_DISTRIBUTION, TOKEN_OPTIMIZATION_CACHE_PREFIX_STABILIZATION, COMPAT_X_CONTRACT_SCHEMA_EVOLUTION
impact: Three architecture files have no plan side (rule 3 violated; only PROOF_DATA is in the known register as ADR-REG-004, still unresolved; the cache-prefix addendum and COMPAT_X file are not registered there). The CI pair gate derives its feature list from the README index (5 rows), so EVOL_X_CHANGE_SAFETY, MCP_SERVER and the three unpaired files are outside the gate and the violation passes CI. Domain pairs are unaffected.
recommendation: Owner decides per file: promote (add plan hub), demote to a satellite of the parent feature, or index in the README; extend the gate to list unindexed files. No product change.

title: Accepted Protocol-v2 remediation (LCI trusted tenant scope, Token Optimization receipt identity) is planned only and not tracked by roadmap or FRZ
affected_invariant: Tenant scope must be authoritative and not mintable from foreign metadata (FRZ-TEN family, TENANT-X)
evidence: E1:roadmap and FRZ checklist contain no mention of LCI, LangChain or TOKEN-OPT (grep counts 0)
impact: Audit findings LANGCHAIN_INDEPENDENCE-01/02 (priority P0: trusted scope injection, provider-hit identity validation) are ACCEPTED / PLANNED and, at the baseline, from_langchain_document and from_legacy_rag_hit take no trusted-scope parameter (code confirms not implemented). TOKEN_OPTIMIZATION findings 01-06 (measurement authority, protected-region integrity, lossy safety, receipt identity with tenant attribution) are likewise planned only. Neither is linked to a roadmap stage, FRZ row or PDC domain, so TENANT-X closure does not cover them. Exploitability is not demonstrated by this audit.
recommendation: Campaign B: check whether tenant/namespace can reach KnowledgeDocument ownership fields via foreign metadata on the compat and legacy hit paths; owner decides whether to schedule the remediation before ARCH-FREEZE or record it as a scoped exclusion.
owner: RAG / LCI owner; Token Optimization owner

title: Feature-local certification claims (Multiplayer, LangChain Independence, Token Optimization, Proof Data) are not reconciled with roadmap, FRZ or IIAC
affected_invariant: Certification semantics decided by IIAC protocol / activation record; roadmap decides formal closure
evidence: E1:grep at SHA: roadmap has 0 hits for Multiplayer, LangChain, LCI, TOKEN, VPI; FRZ checklist has 0 hits for MULTIPLAYER, TOKEN-OPT, LANGCHAIN, LCI-; IIAC_POLICY_ACTIVATION_RECORD.json has 0 hits for MP-FINAL/MULTIPLAYER
impact: Multiplayer states 'ENTERPRISE CERTIFIED / CLOSED' for MP-1..MP-7 and MP-FINAL-2/3/4 and the LCI hub says 'COMPLETE / APPROVED', but none of them is a roadmap stage, none maps to an FRZ family and none appears in the IIAC activation record, so the claims rest on feature-local qualification documents that predate or sit outside IIAC. Their packages (intergrax/collaborative_work, rag/compat, runtime/token_optimization, proof_data) are inputs to closed stages (e.g. SFX reuses Collaborative Work; PDC D8 owns collaborative_work for business artifacts) without a program-level certification row.
recommendation: Operator decides per feature: register as historical/out-of-program (status wording 'feature-local, not IIAC certified') or map to a stage/FRZ family; no re-certification implied by this audit.

title: MCP-SERVER-X is closed with no FRZ mapping and open scoped limitations on identity and reliability
affected_invariant: FRZ-SEC / FRZ-TEN: identity must fail closed; mandatory pre-ARCH-FREEZE gate
impact: Per OD-MCP-07 Option A no FRZ-MCP family exists and the P8 notes conclude no FRZ row has sufficient MCP audit evidence for a note; FRZ-BND-06, FRZ-SEC-01/04 and FRZ-REL rows stay OPEN with R-P8-01 (fail-open identity without harness auth), R-P7-04 (no server-side deadline) and R-P7-06 (harness_auth=None) recorded as limitations. The closure is therefore scoped and its tenant/security rules are not reflected in any FRZ status. This is a documented, accepted limitation, listed so the freeze review sees it.
recommendation: Carry R-P8-01 and R-P7-04/06 into the ARCH-FREEZE handoff as explicit conditions; production auth bypass proof stays with PROD-Q.

title: Feature hubs omit cross-cutting rule cells (tenant/security, configuration, observability, failure/recovery, tests)
affected_invariant: Domain completeness cells (semantic owner, tenant/security, configuration, observability, failure/recovery)
evidence: E1:keyword counts per hub: PROOF_DATA tenant 0 / observability 0 / config 0; EVOL_X tenant 0 / security 0 / config 0 / observability 0; LCI observability 0; SFX failure 0, test evidence none (no code); MULTIPLAYER config section absent
impact: Absent cells (not necessarily absent behavior): PROOF_DATA has no tenant, config or observability rules; EVOL_X hub carries no tenant/security, config or observability rules (passive tool, depends on other owners); LCI has no observability or recovery rule; SFX has no failure/recovery or test evidence yet (pre-implementation, by design); Multiplayer has no configuration section. Related known items: EQOA-A4 findings on missing Security, tenant and state owner docs. Keyword counts are a coarse method, so some rules may live in satellites or dossiers not sampled.
recommendation: Feature owners add one-line 'not applicable because X' or a pointer to the owning domain rule per cell; SFX fills the cells when implementation starts.
